en.title: 9 HUGE Trailers Dropped This Week — You Won't Believe What's Back!
en.summary: From epic game revivals to surprising cinematic reveals, this week's trailer drop is a must-see for any entertainment fan. Get ready for nostalgia and brand-new adventures.
en.body:
This week was packed with reveals, nearly hitting a perfect 10 for trailer drops. We saw the return of beloved gaming franchises alongside significant buzz from early fall film festivals. Plus, M. Night Shyamalan is back with his first post-'Trap' film, and TV thrillers are starting to heat up. Here are the trailers you absolutely need to see.

## 1. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Nintendo dropped a dedicated Direct for the Ocarina of Time remake, giving us an extended gameplay look and an official trailer. While it appears to be a faithful one-to-one recreation, the updated art style has sparked debate among fans. This classic adventure arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5.

## 2. Metroid Ravenous

Following the success of Metroid Dread, the 2D Metroid series continues with Metroid Ravenous. The trailer showcased a vibrant, saturated art direction and a hint of story that has us incredibly hyped. Expect a pissed-off Samus Aran when this lands on Nintendo Switch 2 on January 28.

## 3. Resident Evil – Code Veronica

Summer Game Fest delivered a massive surprise with the trailer for Resident Evil – Code Veronica. This long-awaited remake is finally on the horizon, and the early footage suggests it's a faithful adaptation that fans have been craving. It's a must-watch for any survival horror enthusiast.

## 4. Final Fantasy 7 Revelation

Another major highlight from Summer Game Fest, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is set to expand the beloved RPG's universe. The trailer offered a glimpse into new storylines and character arcs, promising a fresh experience for fans of Cloud and his crew.

## 5. Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4

While details are scarce, the mere mention of Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4 has sent shockwaves through the gaming community. This franchise has a massive legacy, and the anticipation for a new installment is palpable, especially with it being a top trailer for 2026.

## 6. Spyro: A Realm Beyond

Get ready to glide back into adventure with Spyro: A Realm Beyond. This trailer suggests a return to the classic platforming roots that made the purple dragon a star. It’s one of the most anticipated trailers of 2026, promising colorful worlds and playful challenges.

## 7. God of War Laufey

Kratos and Atreus’s saga continues with God of War Laufey. The trailer hints at a new journey filled with Norse mythology and intense combat. With the track record of Santa Monica Studio, this is bound to be an epic continuation of their critically acclaimed series.

## 8. The Blood of Dawnwalker

Built on Unreal Engine 5, The Blood of Dawnwalker looks to be a visually stunning new title. The trailer showcases breathtaking environments and promises a deep narrative, positioning it as a potential breakout hit for PS5 and Xbox players.

## 9. STALKER 2 Cost of Hope

STALKER 2 Cost of Hope has officially arrived, and its trailer is a stark reminder of the atmospheric and dangerous Zone. This Unreal Engine 5 title is available now on PS5 and Xbox, offering a brutal survival experience.

Bottom Line: This week's trailer drops are a powerful mix of long-awaited returns and exciting new prospects across gaming and film.

content_raw: This was very nearly a 10/10 week for trailers. On top of two Nintendo Directs that delivered, the first trailers for the slates of the early fall film festivals like Venice, Telluride, Toronto, and New York have started dropping with some really strong stuff in the mix. On top of that : M. Night Shyamalan’s first post-Trap movie (which some people are already theorizing to be a Sixth Sense sequel) and some early October TV thrillers. Read on for the trailers worth watching this week. (And check out last weeks’ batch too.) The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Adventure through Hyrule and become the Hero of Time when The Legend of #Zelda : Ocarina of Time releases Nov 5 on Nintendo Switch 2. #NintendoDirect pic.twitter.com/rW3r7o2L9r — Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) September 8, 2026 This week’s first Nintendo Direct focusing solely on the Ocarina of Time remake provides an extended gameplay look AND an official trailer. It’s lookin’ pretty one-for-one (mixed feelings, for me!), but we also found 40 differences that you can read all about . There are no bench-sitters on this matter: Do you like the updated art style or not? The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake releases on Switch 2 November 5. Read about everything that was announced at The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintendo Direct . Metroid Ravenous It’s eat or be eaten when Metroid Ravenous, the latest game in the 2D Metroid series, arrives on Nintendo Switch 2 Jan 28! #NintendoDirect pic.twitter.com/3yOE6L5X1R — Nintendo of America (@NintendoAmerica) September 9, 2026 I was doing the Vince McMahon meme, falling back and out of my chair (OK, I didn’t), when this trailer aired in the second-day Nintendo Direct. Of everything shown off, the 2D Metroid Ravenous, the followup to 2018’s Metroid Dread, had me (and my colleagues live-reacting on NVC ) most hyped on everything from the saturated art direction to the brief story tease. Pissed-off Samus, coming through! My girl is hungry! Metroid Ravenous will release on Nintendo Switch 2 on January 28, 2027. Read about everything else announced during the Nintendo Direct .
